# PART 2 – The claim, its estimand and its causal graph {#part-2-the-claim-its-estimand-and-its-causal-graph .darkslide background-color="rgba(0,0,0,0)"}

::: {.partlabel}
Part 2 · 90 minutes
:::

::: notes
Part two. The case of the day is a survey study, and a careful one: more than a hundred thousand respondents in sixteen countries, asked how much they trust their parliament and what they think immigration does to their country. Five analysts in Multi100 reanalysed one of its claims from the same file, all five found evidence for it, and still their estimates differed by a factor of two. This part explains how that can happen. We go inside the paper first, then step back to two studies that show how often disagreement among analysts is disagreement about the question. Then we build the two tools that state a question precisely, the estimand and the causal graph, and use both on our claim, where the graph asks what each control in the model actually is.
:::
